author: WP03
summary: A dense account of Game (events, properties, override points, Exit/Exiting, disposal versus destruction), the clock (catch-up, IsRunningSlowly, ResetElapsedTime), GameTime, components, services, GameWindow, GraphicsDeviceManager, supporting types and the exception boundary. Most mechanics are current at TARGET, but the browser loop (now Asyncify, Run returns), controller and audio teardown, GameWindow's SDL coupling, several XNA-parity claims (ExitingEventArgs, ResetElapsedTime) and renderer counts are stale. The Development internals pages already traced startup, frame and shutdown in depth; the API-semantics residue, edge cases, XNA 4.0 comparisons and evidence caveats went into five framework deep dives plus two additive expansions of the game-loop guide.

concepts.section: Game: base class, not framework-owned entry point
concepts.text: Game derives from System::Object and System::IDisposable; its brief calls it the base class that provides the XNA-style game loop, services, window, content and components, and CNA has no engine-owned main().

concepts.section: Game: base class, not framework-owned entry point
concepts.text: Game's four events Activated, Deactivated, Disposed and Exiting are all typed System::EventHandler<System::EventArgs> and are raised with the game as sender (the On... virtuals ignore the sender argument).

concepts.section: Game: base class, not framework-owned entry point
concepts.text: CNA declares an empty ExitingEventArgs, but Game::Exiting is typed with plain EventArgs, nothing constructs the dedicated type, and its only tests check default construction and derivation.

concepts.section: Game: base class, not framework-owned entry point
concepts.text: The claim that ExitingEventArgs matches real XNA's public API and that XNA has the same quirk is only half right: XNA 4.0 types Game.Exiting as EventHandler<EventArgs>, but no ExitingEventArgs type exists in the XNA 4.0 assemblies, so the type is a CNA-specific addition (as CNA's AUDIT.md lists it).

target.evidence: XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (.event Exiting); AUDIT.md (ExitingEventArgs row)

concepts.section: Properties, and one that is deliberately not settable from outside
concepts.text: Game exposes Components, Content, GraphicsDevice (get-only, taken from the registered IGraphicsDeviceService when it has a device, else the game's own member; no setter), InactiveSleepTime, IsFixedTimeStep, IsMouseVisible, LaunchParameters, TargetElapsedTime, Services and Window through getXProperty()/setXProperty().

concepts.section: Properties, and one that is deliberately not settable from outside
concepts.text: Property guards at TARGET: a negative InactiveSleepTime and a non-positive TargetElapsedTime throw std::out_of_range; InactiveSleepTime (default 20 ms) is stored but never applied by the loop, whereas XNA 4.0's Tick sleeps for it while inactive; IsMouseVisible reaches the platform only with a window and a mouse service.
tokens: read by nothing in the loop

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (setInactiveSleepTimeProperty, setTargetElapsedTimeProperty, setIsMouseVisibleProperty); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::Tick Thread.Sleep(inactiveSleepTime))

concepts.note: TARGET extension of the Bible's property list; the InactiveSleepTime gap is also recorded on the runtime module page.

concepts.section: Properties, and one that is deliberately not settable from outside
concepts.text: IsActive is get-only in public; its setter is private (FNA's internal set has no C++ equivalent), returns early when unchanged and raises Activated/Deactivated through the protected virtuals; it changes only in BeforeLoop, focus events and mobile lifecycle events.

concepts.section: Properties, and one that is deliberately not settable from outside
concepts.text: OnActivated and OnDeactivated assert the game is not disposed, so a focus change delivered to a disposed game throws std::runtime_error, while OnExiting has no such check.
concepts.note: TARGET detail found while verifying the IsActive claim.

concepts.section: The override points
concepts.text: A concrete game overrides Initialize, LoadContent, UnloadContent, Update(GameTime&), Draw(const GameTime&), BeginRun/EndRun, BeginDraw/EndDraw, OnExiting/OnActivated/OnDeactivated, ShowMissingRequirementMessage and the protected Dispose(bool); the base implementations of Initialize, Update, Draw, BeginDraw and EndDraw do real framework work.
concepts.note: The Bible's list omitted the three On... event raisers.

concepts.section: The override points
concepts.text: BeginDraw() returning false skips both Draw and EndDraw for that tick; GraphicsDeviceManager returns false when it has no device (and when the renderer's CanBeginDrawEXT refuses).

concepts.section: The override points
concepts.text: ShowMissingRequirementMessage can be overridden but no CNA code calls it; XNA 4.0's Game.Run catches NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException and NoAudioHardwareException, offers them to it and rethrows on false, so a port relying on it must catch in main() instead.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (only definition, no caller in the TARGET tree); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::RunGame catch handlers)

concepts.section: The override points
concepts.text: UnloadContent() is live on explicit shutdown: Game::Initialize subscribes it to the device service's DeviceDisposing event, and GraphicsDeviceManager::Dispose(bool) raises that event although the game-attached manager does not own the device; only the device delete stays ownership-gated, so the public Game::Dispose() reaches UnloadContent exactly once.

concepts.section: The override points
concepts.text: The component contract is separate from the game's: explicit game disposal disposes each IDisposable component, and DrawableGameComponent::Dispose(bool) calls that component's own UnloadContent(); ordinary destruction executes neither path.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Exit() only sets RunApplication to false and sets suppressDraw_; it does not raise Exiting and disposes nothing.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: An Exit() from Update does not end the current tick: remaining catch-up updates still run and only that tick's draw is skipped; the loop checks the flag between ticks and RunLoop raises Exiting after the loop ends.
tokens: only the draw of that tick is skipped

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Desktop Run order: DoInitialize once (manager CreateDevice, Initialize, component categorization), BeginRun, BeforeLoop (IsActive true, Activated), RunLoop ticks while RunApplication, OnExiting (Exiting), then EndRun and AfterLoop.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: The statement that DoInitialize initializes gamepad support is false at TARGET: Game acquires no controller subsystem; the platform starts it lazily on first gamepad or joystick use.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (DoInitialize comment on the ~1.9 s udev enumeration; PollEvents gamepad gate)

concepts.note: Removed eager acquisition; the correct statement is already on the startup trace and architecture pages.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Because Exiting is raised before Run() calls EndRun(), an Exiting handler runs before an EndRun() override; Exiting is a non-cancellable loop-boundary notification.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Calling Exit() before Run() does not bypass the lifecycle: initialization, BeginRun and BeforeLoop run, the loop performs zero ticks, Exiting is raised, then EndRun and AfterLoop.
concepts.note: Untested edge.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Run() never resets RunApplication: a second Run() after exit skips initialization, reruns BeginRun/BeforeLoop, performs zero ticks and raises Exiting again unless application code sets the public flag back to true; after Dispose() Run() throws.
concepts.note: Untested edge.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: RunOneFrame() performs one-time initialization and one Tick() only, never BeginRun, BeforeLoop, EndRun, AfterLoop or OnExiting, so IsActive stays false under it (a trap for hosts and tests).

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Browser builds raise Exiting only when the frame body observes RunApplication == false, then clear the loop slot.

concepts.section: Exit() requests a stop; Exiting describes the completed loop
concepts.text: Tick() is public: calling it without Run() or RunOneFrame() skips DoInitialize entirely (no CreateDevice, Initialize or LoadContent) and the first call only seeds the performance counter before waiting a full target span.
concepts.note: TARGET detail found while verifying the run-mode claims.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: Dispose(true) disposes every IDisposable component, then the content manager, then the resolved graphics-device service, and sets the disposed flag only after that; the public wrapper then raises Disposed.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: The statement that Dispose(true) also shuts down the SDL gamepad subsystem (and that a scoped game relies on wider SDL shutdown for it) is stale: Game no longer acquires that subsystem and the platform releases it when destroyed.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (Dispose(bool) comment: nothing to release for controllers)

concepts.note: Obsolete controller handling from an earlier revision.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: Explicit disposal yields two distinct UnloadContent() calls on two objects: the drawable component's via its Dispose(bool), and the game's via DeviceDisposing, which runs after the content manager was already disposed.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: The destructor calls Dispose(false), which only marks the game disposed (no component, content or device-service disposal), and member destructors run afterwards.
tokens: which only marks the game disposed

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: The claim that the destructor shuts down audio after Dispose(false) is stale: at TARGET ~Game calls Dispose(false) and then uninstalls its platform from the ambient accessor; there is no audio shutdown call in Game.
concepts.note: Audio init/shutdown moved out of Game at TARGET.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: ContentManager's destructor is defaulted rather than calling its public Dispose(); the asset cache is simply destroyed with the member.
tokens: The content manager's destructor is defaulted

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: DrawableGameComponent has no destructor; ~GameComponent's virtual Dispose(false) call resolves to GameComponent::Dispose(false) during base destruction, so destruction never dispatches a drawable component's UnloadContent().

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: The disposed flag is written only after all true-path cleanup succeeds, so an exception from a component, the content manager or the device service aborts the rest, leaves the game not disposed and suppresses Disposed; a later Dispose() restarts (an UnloadContent that threw is called again).
tokens: written only after all true-path cleanup succeeded
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP03-i002 (CNA-BUG-020).

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: The public wrapper raises Disposed even when Dispose(bool) returns early, so every repeated Dispose() re-raises the event; UnloadContent is not repeated because the manager's own guard makes DeviceDisposing one-time.
tokens: on every call, including repeated ones
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP03-i001 (CNA-BUG-019).

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: A Disposed handler that calls Dispose() on the notifying game re-enters the wrapper, which raises Disposed again: unbounded recursion (EventHandler::Raise invokes a snapshot), and XNA 4.0 has no guard against it either.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (Dispose); sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9 System/EventHandler.hpp (Raise snapshot); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::Dispose(bool))

concepts.note: The Bible said the handler re-enters; the consequence is unbounded recursion.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: The repeated-Disposed wrapper shape is recorded by CNA's own test comment as FNA-faithful, and XNA 4.0 also raises Disposed on every disposing call (from inside Dispose(bool), with no disposed guard).

target.evidence: GameTests.cpp (comment on RepeatedDisposeDoesNotReinvokeUnloadContent); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::Dispose(bool))

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: Evidence: repeated public disposal is covered (GameTest.RepeatedDisposeDoesNotReinvokeUnloadContent, GraphicsDeviceManagerTest.RepeatedDisposeDoesNotReraiseDeviceDisposing); no test exercises ordinary destruction, handler exceptions or re-entrant disposal.

concepts.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
concepts.text: Compared with XNA 4.0, CNA iterates the live component collection (XNA a snapshot array), disposes the ContentManager before the device service (XNA only unloads it in the DeviceDisposing handler), raises Disposed from the public wrapper (XNA from Dispose(bool)), and a disposed component is not removed from Game.Components.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (Dispose(bool)); modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp (Dispose, disposed check); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::Dispose(bool), DeviceDisposing handler)

concepts.note: Comparison added while verifying the disposal claims.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: Game carries FNA's adaptive-sleep timing loop: a 128-entry previousSleepTimes_ ring masked with SLEEP_TIME_MASK, a worstCaseSleepPrecision_ estimate updated by UpdateEstimatedSleepPrecision (samples capped at 4 ms), AdvanceElapsedTime driving pacing against TargetElapsedTime, capped by MaxElapsedTime.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: Two list pairs, updateableComponents_/currentlyUpdatingComponents_ and drawableComponents_/currentlyDrawingComponents_, guard against a component mutating the collection during its own Update or Draw.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: The Emscripten path was described as a registered callback because a blocking while loop is not viable in a browser; at TARGET RunLoop is a blocking loop that suspends the same Wasm stack with Asyncify, awaiting requestAnimationFrame between frame bodies.
concepts.note: The site's frame trace already explains the current Asyncify design, which replaces the Bible's rationale.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: Browser clock: the frame body uses the platform's millisecond ticks (not the desktop performance counter), is paced by the browser, and has no sleep/spin ring.
concepts.note: Bible named SDL_GetTicks; TARGET goes through the platform.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: The browser frame body always drains fixed TargetElapsedTime-sized steps and ignores IsFixedTimeStep.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: Lag handling differs: desktop clamps to 500 ms and uses the IsRunningSlowly hysteresis; the browser clamps each delta to 250 ms and forces IsRunningSlowly false every step.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: Control methods on the web: the frame body consults neither suppressDraw_ nor forceElapsedTimeToZero_, so SuppressDraw() and ResetElapsedTime() have no effect there.
tokens: SuppressDraw() and ResetElapsedTime() have no effect

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: Draw cadence differs: the desktop tick attempts one draw per tick, while the browser frame body draws only if at least one update ran.
tokens: Only if at least one update ran

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: The claim that the browser's registered loop never returns so EndRun and AfterLoop never run is false at TARGET: RunLoop returns after the frame body clears the loop slot and Run() calls EndRun and AfterLoop.
concepts.note: The TARGET-correct lifecycle is written on the Game class deep dive (#browser) and the frame trace.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: The browser loop state is one static slot (s_emLoopState), so one Game runs its loop per process; destroying that game during Run clears the slot and logs an error.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: A frame-body exception is caught, logged and ends the browser loop without raising Exiting; Run() then calls EndRun and AfterLoop and returns normally, so the exception never reaches main().
tokens: fatal exception in Emscripten main loop
concepts.note: TARGET detail found while verifying the browser row of the table.

concepts.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
concepts.text: The older object-lifetime hazard of Emscripten's non-returning main-loop registration combined with the WASM exception mode (a stack-allocated game destroyed under the loop) belongs to a replaced implementation.
concepts.note: docs/emscripten-mainloop-game-lifetime.md at TARGET records the former emscripten_set_main_loop design as replaced by Asyncify; a stack-allocated Game is valid now.

concepts.section: Two global debug keys hidden in the ordinary event pump
concepts.text: PollEvents sends every event through the input bridge first and then reserves non-repeated F9 (renderer DebugSimulateContextLoss) and F10 (DebugRestoreContext); a game binding either key gets both its key state and the framework action.
concepts.note: The Bible's comparison with FNA (no equivalent hotkeys) could not be checked here (no FNA source available) and is not published.

concepts.section: Two global debug keys hidden in the ordinary event pump
concepts.text: The claim that most renderers inherit empty debug hooks and only EasyGL and DirectX 9 make the keys consequential is stale: at TARGET EasyGL, DirectX 9, DirectX 11, DirectX 12, Direct2D and WebGPU declare non-empty overrides and GDI overrides with empty bodies.
concepts.note: Per-renderer loss/restore behaviour (EasyGL synchronous vs asynchronous, DirectX 9 transitions) is renderer-specific and left to the renderer pages; not re-verified here.

concepts.section: Two small, explicitly-marked CNA extensions
concepts.text: RunApplication is a public CNAEXT bool documented as the internal loop flag matching the FNA/XNA Game shape; Exit() clears it and only application code sets it back.

concepts.section: Two small, explicitly-marked CNA extensions
concepts.text: getTargetFPSProperty(), getTargetMsFrameTimeProperty() and static fpsToMillisecondsPerFrame(intcs) are CNAEXT helpers kept for existing CNA examples; they derive from TargetElapsedTime (about 59.99988 FPS at the default) and return 0 for non-positive input.

concepts.section: What happens when a frame runs long
concepts.text: Under the fixed step, Tick accumulates wall-clock time and drains it in whole TargetElapsedTime steps, calling Update once per step before a single Draw.

concepts.section: What happens when a frame runs long
concepts.text: The quoted catch-up listing (ElapsedGameTime set to the target before the loop, TotalGameTime advanced before Update) no longer matches TARGET: the first update sees zero elapsed time and TotalGameTime advances after Update returns, as measured on XNA 4.0.
concepts.note: The current clock rule is on the frame trace (#xna-time) and the GameTime deep dive.

concepts.section: What happens when a frame runs long
concepts.text: Worked numbers: the default target is 166,667 ticks (16.6667 ms); an accumulator of 50.5 ms runs three updates of 16.6667 ms each and leaves 0.4999 ms, while exactly 50.0 ms runs only two, since three steps need 50.0001 ms.
concepts.note: The Bible's '50 ms gives three updates' is off by the 100 ns tick rounding.

concepts.section: What happens when a frame runs long
concepts.text: Immediately before drawing, ElapsedGameTime is rewritten to TargetElapsedTime x stepCount in integer ticks, so Draw sees the whole catch-up (500,001 ticks after three steps) while each Update saw one step; intentional accounting, not an unstable clock.

concepts.section: What happens when a frame runs long
concepts.text: Update must be safe to run several times between draws and must never assume one update per draw; a frame counter belongs in Draw.
tokens: never assume one update per draw

concepts.section: What happens when a frame runs long
concepts.text: At the default target the 500 ms clamp allows at most 29 updates in one tick, because 30 steps of 166,667 ticks exceed 500 ms by 100 ns.
concepts.note: Corrects the audit's '~30 catch-up updates'.

concepts.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
concepts.text: IsRunningSlowly is decided by an updateFrameLag_ counter: each tick adds stepCount-1, the flag turns on at 5, turns off only when the counter is back at 0, and single-step ticks decrement it by one.

concepts.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
concepts.text: A single 50 ms stutter (three updates) never sets IsRunningSlowly, but a single tick with six or more updates (about 100 ms or more) sets it at once; the claim that it needs several consecutive lagging ticks is too strong.
tokens: One stall of 100 ms or more

concepts.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
concepts.text: Clearing takes one more normal tick than the counter's value because the check runs before the decrement; after a 500 ms stall (29 steps) the flag stays set for 28 normal ticks and clears on the 29th.
tokens: one more normal tick than the counter's value

concepts.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
concepts.text: The flag is written after the tick's updates, so the updates that caused the lag do not see it (that tick's Draw does); variable step never writes it and the browser forces it false; it is a smoothed signal, not a per-frame one.
concepts.note: Expansion wp03-game-loop-isrunningslowly added to the user guide, whose table overstated the rule.

concepts.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
concepts.text: No regression test pins the hysteresis: GameTimeTests only exercises GameTime's constructors and getters, and the timing tests drive single frames.

concepts.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
concepts.text: The counter follows the clock loop CNA took from FNA; XNA 4.0 uses a different heuristic (two 'ticks since running slowly' counters, true while the older of the last two multi-step ticks is fewer than 20 ticks back, assigned before each Update), so the two can disagree tick by tick and no oracle compares them.

target.evidence: XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::Tick updatesSinceRunningSlowly1/2, drawRunningSlowly)

concepts.note: The Bible said correctness rests on matching FNA; compatibility with XNA 4.0 is the relevant contract.

concepts.section: ResetElapsedTime() under fixed timestep
concepts.text: ResetElapsedTime() sets forceElapsedTimeToZero_ only when IsFixedTimeStep is false; under the default fixed step it does nothing and nothing in the fixed-step branch reads the flag.
tokens: ResetElapsedTime() does nothing in fixed-step mode

concepts.section: ResetElapsedTime() under fixed timestep
concepts.text: The claim that the fixed-step no-op matches XNA's documented behaviour is wrong for XNA 4.0: its ResetElapsedTime sets the zero-elapsed flag in both modes and resets its running-slowly counters, and Tick zeroes the measured elapsed time before branching, discarding a load-screen spike in fixed-step mode too.
tokens: This is a divergence from XNA 4.0

target.evidence: XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (Game::ResetElapsedTime, Game::Tick)

concepts.note: Issue candidate WP03-i004.

concepts.section: ResetElapsedTime() under fixed timestep
concepts.text: Calling ResetElapsedTime() after a blocking load inside Update under the fixed step therefore still produces the catch-up burst on the next tick (up to 29 updates); in variable step the next update sees zero and TotalGameTime does not advance.

concepts.section: The base Update and Draw calls are framework work, not optional ceremony
concepts.text: Game::Update snapshots and updates enabled components and ends with FrameworkDispatcher::Update(); a derived Update that skips it stops dynamic-stream dispatch, microphone checks, media-player transitions and touch updates.
tokens: A derived Update that does not call Game::Update

concepts.section: The base Update and Draw calls are framework work, not optional ceremony
concepts.text: Call the base Update exactly once per step; a port that replaces the component loop must still call FrameworkDispatcher::Update() itself, and calling both pumps those services twice.

concepts.section: The base Update and Draw calls are framework work, not optional ceremony
concepts.text: Game::Draw draws visible components in ascending DrawOrder; an override that never calls it suppresses every DrawableGameComponent.

concepts.section: The base Update and Draw calls are framework work, not optional ceremony
concepts.text: Presentation happens in EndDraw after Draw returns, through the registered manager; application Draw() should not call Present().
tokens: Do not call Present() in Draw()

concepts.section: GameTime: three fields, one privileged writer
concepts.text: GameTime holds TotalGameTime and ElapsedGameTime (TimeSpan) and IsRunningSlowly (bool) with public getters and private setters unlocked by friend class Game, mirroring XNA 4.0's internal setters; three public constructors build arbitrary values.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GameTime.hpp; XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (GameTime assembly-internal setters)

concepts.section: GameTime: three fields, one privileged writer
concepts.text: The claim that code can never falsify a GameTime is too strong: copy assignment is public and Update receives Game's own clock object by non-const reference, so assigning to the parameter overwrites the state Tick continues from (in C# it would only rebind a local).

target.evidence: GameTime.hpp (implicit copy assignment); modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (Tick passes gameTime_); syntax-checked assignment

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: GameComponent implements IGameComponent, IUpdateable, System::IComparable<GameComponent> and System::IDisposable; it knows its owning Game, is Enabled by default and has an UpdateOrder of 0.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: GameComponent::CompareTo returns other.UpdateOrder - this.UpdateOrder (inverted sign); Game never uses it, it is not an XNA 4.0 member (XNA's GameComponent implements only IGameComponent, IUpdateable and IDisposable), it is not marked CNAEXT, and the subtraction can overflow at extreme orders.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/GameComponent.cpp (CompareTo); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (GameComponent class declaration)

concepts.note: The Bible's attribution to FNA was not verifiable here; the XNA 4.0 absence is.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: Game's insertion keeps updateables in ascending UpdateOrder and drawables in ascending DrawOrder, inserting before the first strictly greater value so equal orders keep insertion order.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: DrawableGameComponent adds IDrawable: a GraphicsDevice getter (forwarding to the game, usable before initialization unlike XNA's), DrawOrder and Visible.
tokens: works before the component is initialized

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/DrawableGameComponent.cpp (getGraphicsDeviceProperty); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (DrawableGameComponent.get_GraphicsDevice throws before Initialize)

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: DrawableGameComponent::Initialize() calls LoadContent() once (guarded by initialized_); in the ordinary loop this happens after DoInitialize configured the existing device, so it is a sound first load point.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: The private OnDeviceCreated exists but is subscribed to nothing, so a drawable component never reloads on a later DeviceCreated (and has no DeviceDisposing hook); XNA 4.0's version requires a device service, hooks all four device events and reloads/unloads with the device.

target.evidence: DrawableGameComponent.cpp (OnDeviceCreated, Initialize); XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game assembly (IL disassembly, not a CNA file) (DrawableGameComponent.Initialize)

concepts.note: Issue candidate WP03-i009.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: IGameComponent has one pure virtual Initialize(); IUpdateable and IDrawable each expose an enabled/visible getter, an order getter, a changed-event pair returned as EventHandler& and the Update or Draw method.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: Component setters raise the public event and then call the empty protected On...Changed virtual; in XNA 4.0 the protected method raises the event, so an XNA override that skips its base suppresses the event while a CNA override cannot.

concepts.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
concepts.text: GameComponent::Dispose(true) raises the component's Disposed but does not remove it from Game.Components (XNA 4.0 removes it first), so a disposed component keeps being updated and drawn until removed.

concepts.section: A self-contained DrawableGameComponent
concepts.text: A frame counter is the natural first DrawableGameComponent, but it must count in Draw: counting Update calls under the fixed step measures the update rate; summing Draw's ElapsedGameTime gives the game time the drawn frames covered.
concepts.note: The Bible's counter incremented in Update.

concepts.section: A self-contained DrawableGameComponent
concepts.text: GameComponentCollection::Add(IGameComponent*) borrows; a derived game's members are destroyed before its Game base and Components, so a member component should be removed in the derived destructor while both are alive, which makes Game drop it from its lists and its order-change subscriptions.

concepts.section: A self-contained DrawableGameComponent
concepts.text: Game::Dispose() disposes components but does not remove them or their order tokens, the collection's destructor raises no events, and setters have no disposed guard; a component that survives the game's destruction keeps a callback into it and its next order change is a use-after-free.

concepts.section: A self-contained DrawableGameComponent
concepts.text: setDrawOrderProperty(1000) orders the counter after other components, but it appears on top of the game's own drawing only if the derived Draw calls Game::Draw(gameTime) last.

concepts.text: The example's remark that TimeSpan has no operator+= is stale: Sharp Runtime's TimeSpan declares operator+= (next @ 41b918c9).

concepts.section: GameComponentCollection: an event-raising collection, plus a real C++ iterator surface
concepts.text: GameComponentCollection raises ComponentAdded/ComponentRemoved (EventHandler<GameComponentCollectionEventArgs>) around Add, Insert, Remove, RemoveAt and Clear, with IndexOf, Contains and operator[] for queries.

concepts.section: GameComponentCollection: an event-raising collection, plus a real C++ iterator surface
concepts.text: Because C#'s IEnumerable has no direct C++ equivalent, the collection adds CNAEXT size_type/iterator/const_iterator aliases and begin()/end() for range-based for; the non-const iterators write raw pointers without raising events.

concepts.section: GameComponentCollection: an event-raising collection, plus a real C++ iterator surface
concepts.text: Collection edge semantics at TARGET: duplicates throw std::invalid_argument (a null entry can be stored once), bounds are checked with std::out_of_range, Remove erases before raising ComponentRemoved while Clear raises for every entry before emptying, and the shared_ptr overloads (CNAEXT) own their components.
tokens: Cannot Add Same Component Multiple Times
concepts.note: TARGET extension of the section.

concepts.section: GameServiceContainer: type-keyed lookup without C# reflection
concepts.text: GameServiceContainer keys a std::unordered_map<std::type_index, void*> by typeid of the template argument of AddService/GetService/RemoveService, which delegate to non-template type_info overloads, because C++ lacks the reflection behind C#'s Type-keyed dictionary.

concepts.section: GameServiceContainer: type-keyed lookup without C# reflection
concepts.text: Copy construction and assignment are deleted ('services are registered by pointer identity') while moves are defaulted, all CNAEXT: a container can be relocated but never duplicated into a second set of pointers.

concepts.section: GameServiceContainer: type-keyed lookup without C# reflection
concepts.text: The template argument is the key: AddService(&impl) without an explicit interface deduces the concrete type, and the non-template AddService(typeid, void*) skips the base-pointer adjustment, so lookups through a non-primary base would use a wrong address.
tokens: The key is the template argument
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.section: Registering and consuming a service
concepts.text: The service pattern from GameServiceContainerTests: register an implementation under its interface with AddService<ISaveGameService>(&impl) and fetch it anywhere with GetService<ISaveGameService>(), which returns null when absent.

concepts.section: Registering and consuming a service
concepts.text: AddService with a null provider throws std::invalid_argument, and so does a second registration for the same type; there is no last-write-wins, so RemoveService<T>() must come first. The container owns nothing.

concepts.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
concepts.text: Where FNA has an abstract GameWindow with per-platform subclasses, CNA keeps one concrete facade; at TARGET it delegates to CNA::Platform::IPlatformWindow of the selected platform implementation rather than being SDL3-backed, and it does not own the native window.
concepts.note: The Bible's 'one SDL-backed class' predates the platform layer.

concepts.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
concepts.text: GameWindow exposes AllowUserResizing, ClientBounds, CurrentOrientation, Handle, ScreenDeviceName, Title and the ClientSizeChanged/OrientationChanged/ScreenDeviceNameChanged events; OnActivated/OnDeactivated/OnPaint exist with empty bodies and no caller.

concepts.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
concepts.text: EXT-suffixed members mark non-XNA additions on an XNA-shaped class: GetNativeWindowHandleEXT (the SDL-typed GetNativeSdlWindowEXT no longer exists), IsBorderlessEXT (suffix only, no CNAEXT marker), MinimizeEXT/RestoreEXT (XNA has no minimize/restore), plus FileDropEXT/TextDropEXT and SetLogicalSizeProviderEXT.

concepts.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
concepts.text: Window setters are not best-effort: GameWindow catches nothing, and on the SDL3 platform every failing SDL setter call becomes a PlatformException (a std::runtime_error).
concepts.note: Bible: std::runtime_error raised by GameWindow via SDL errors.

concepts.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
concepts.text: The deliberate exception is the client-bounds read: on SDL3 it never throws and returns the last successfully queried rectangle (browser canvas start-up, native teardown); GraphicsDevice::UpdateViewportFromWindow logs and keeps the previous surface on a refused query.
concepts.note: Moved from GameWindow to the platform window.

concepts.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
concepts.text: The native window handle is a borrowed view, not an ownership transfer: it views the device-created window, is empty without a window, must never be destroyed by game code and must not be kept across explicit graphics-device disposal.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: GraphicsDeviceManager implements IGraphicsDeviceManager's three methods (BeginDraw returning bool, CreateDevice, EndDraw) that Game::BeginDraw/EndDraw delegate to; BeginDraw returns false without a device, so Game skips Draw/EndDraw instead of crashing.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: The manager keeps FNA's five events (DeviceCreated, DeviceDisposing, DeviceReset, DeviceResetting, PreparingDeviceSettings); forwarded reset and disposing events report the manager as sender while DeviceCreated forwards its sender, an FNA asymmetry preserved on purpose.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: FindBestDevice, RankDevices and CanResetDevice are not a selection pipeline: no manager path invokes them; defaults build a default record, do nothing, and report whether a device exists, so overriding RankDevices changes nothing.
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP03-i010.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: Construction registers the manager's two services without ApplyChanges(); DoInitialize's CreateDevice() is the single initial pass (profile, presentation mode, in-place Reset, viewport), and the manager subscribes to the device's reset events only after that settle-in reset, so start-up reports DeviceCreated and a later ApplyChanges forwards the pair once.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: ApplyChanges() returns early unless a preference changed (every setter marks the change); because the manager already points at the game's device, ApplyChanges() in the derived constructor reconfigures immediately and CreateDevice() repeats it, the double reconfiguration the source calls a visible start-up flicker.
tokens: returns immediately unless a preference changed
concepts.note: TARGET extension of the section.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: CNAEXT enum class PresentationMode (Letterbox, Overscan, Stretch, NativeBackBuffer, FixedHeightDynamicWidth) expresses the game's requested policy when the virtual back buffer and the display differ in aspect ratio; it is a manager-side request, not a promise that every renderer implements it.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: XNA never needed presentation modes for the Xbox 360 and desktop windows of its era; CNA's targets (browser canvases, rotating phones, arbitrary desktop windows) make it a genuinely new, clearly marked subsystem. The default at TARGET is Letterbox so the Viewport equals the back buffer as in XNA and FNA.
concepts.note: An earlier revision defaulted to FixedHeightDynamicWidth.

concepts.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
concepts.text: Setting 1280x720 and PresentationMode::Letterbox in the constructor, before CreateDevice, gives a fixed logical coordinate space: on a renderer that implements Letterbox a resized window shows bars and draw calls stay in 1280x720.

concepts.section: Vertical retrace is a presentation preference, not the fixed timestep
concepts.text: SynchronizeWithVerticalRetrace defaults to true and maps to PresentInterval::One or Immediate, which Reset forwards to the renderer as swap interval 1 or 0; it is independent of IsFixedTimeStep, and turning one off does not turn the other off.
tokens: Turning one off does not turn the other off

concepts.section: Vertical retrace is a presentation preference, not the fixed timestep
concepts.text: PresentInterval::Two cannot be expressed through the Boolean; a PreparingDeviceSettings handler can set it (the args hand over a const reference, so CNA adds getGraphicsDeviceInformationEXT()), the device maps it to swap interval 2, and driver acceptance is renderer-specific.
concepts.note: The per-renderer interval matrix (SDL Renderer, EasyGL, DirectX 9 values) was not re-verified here and is left to the renderer pages.

concepts.section: Vertical retrace is a presentation preference, not the fixed timestep
concepts.text: The claim that the Vulkan renderer ignores runtime swap-interval changes (inheriting a no-op SetSwapInterval, so disabling vsync after construction leaves FIFO) is false at TARGET: VulkanRenderer::SetSwapInterval records the request and rebuilds the swapchain.
concepts.note: The site's Vulkan internals page already states the current behaviour; issue candidate WP03-i013 records it as absent.

concepts.section: Vertical retrace is a presentation preference, not the fixed timestep
concepts.text: The manager's SynchronizeWithVerticalRetrace property reports the requested Boolean; it is not an observation of the active present mode.
tokens: not an observation of the active present mode

concepts.section: Format and fullscreen preferences: three fields, three kinds of truth
concepts.text: The manager's back-buffer format starts as Color, depth as Depth24 and fullscreen false, while a bare PresentationParameters starts with depth None; all three preferences are copied into the reset parameters.
concepts.note: The Bible's 'FNA uses the same defaults' was not verifiable here and is not published.

concepts.section: Format and fullscreen preferences: three fields, three kinds of truth
concepts.text: After ApplyChanges the preferences mean different things: the manager getters report the request, while the device's PresentationParameters report formats normalized through the renderer (GetAppliedBackBufferFormatEXT); UpdatePresentationFormatEXT is overridden by ten families at TARGET, not only DirectX 9.
concepts.note: Bible: only D3D9 overrides and thirteen other products report success blindly.

concepts.section: Format and fullscreen preferences: three fields, three kinds of truth
concepts.text: Fullscreen is a window operation applied by EndScreenDeviceChange and again by the device reset; on SDL3 a refused request throws PlatformException (the old 'cleared and non-fatal' behaviour is gone, though a source comment still says so), the web defers it to a user gesture, and a true property is requested state, not proof.

concepts.section: Format and fullscreen preferences: three fields, three kinds of truth
concepts.text: The DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 renderers never call DXGI SetFullscreenState, so fullscreen there is the platform window's state, never DXGI exclusive mode.

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: LaunchParameters parses the process arguments into key/value pairs and publicly inherits std::unordered_map<std::string,std::string> (so it is a standard container, without a virtual destructor).

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: LaunchParameters reads arguments only on Windows (CommandLineToArgvW) and Linux/Android (/proc/self/cmdline) and is empty elsewhere; parsing strips leading / and -, needs a ':' neither first nor last, keeps the first key, and Add ignores duplicates where FNA throws.
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: TitleContainer is static-only; OpenStream(path) returns std::unique_ptr<System::IO::Stream>, resolves relative names against TitleLocation with XNA case-insensitive matching and throws std::runtime_error when nothing opens.

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: TitleLocation resolves and caches the base path and exposes it as both getPathProperty() and a bare Path() kept to match the XNA property name.

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: TitleContainer/TitleLocation are an independent direct-file facility: ContentManager does not open assets through them at TARGET.

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: FrameworkDispatcher is static-only and drives dynamic sound streams, microphones, MediaPlayer and touch through one Update(), called by base Game::Update after components on every step.

concepts.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
concepts.text: FrameworkDispatcher's stream list is mutex-protected but streams are updated from a snapshot with the lock released, so a BufferNeeded handler can dispose its own stream without deadlocking; a thread-safety addition beyond FNA's single-threaded assumption.

concepts.section: One catch clause for the framework boundary
concepts.text: The runtime module translates nothing into an XNA exception hierarchy and throws only standard types; at TARGET it has 21 explicit throw sites (std::out_of_range, std::invalid_argument, std::runtime_error, std::logic_error, std::bad_alloc), not the 30 counted earlier.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src and include (grep of throw statements at TARGET)

concepts.note: Window setter throws moved to the platform module.

concepts.section: One catch clause for the framework boundary
concepts.text: Elsewhere two exception families exist: PlatformException, ContentLoadException and the parse/XNB-write exceptions derive from std::runtime_error, while the graphics device exceptions, CNAException and the audio, gamer-services, network, sensor, engine-layer and pipeline exceptions derive from System::Exception.
concepts.note: The graphics device exceptions derive from System::Exception at TARGET.

concepts.section: One catch clause for the framework boundary
concepts.text: System::Exception derives from std::exception, not std::runtime_error, so catch (const std::runtime_error&) misses the System family and catch (const System::Exception&) misses standard failures; only catch (const std::exception&) spans both.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9 modules/core/include/System/Exception.hpp (class Exception : public std::exception)

concepts.section: One catch clause for the framework boundary
concepts.text: Catch narrowly where recovery depends on the exact contract and use std::exception only for a top-level log-and-exit boundary; Run() logs and rethrows, while browser frame exceptions never reach main().

concepts.section: What this buys a porting engineer
concepts.text: The timing, component, service and window layer an XNA Game subclass depends on is present under the same names, so a subclass using only the public XNA surface ports by translating syntax; behaviour differences (inert hooks, unapplied properties, clock heuristics) still need review.
concepts.note: Representation claim; behavioural caveats are listed on the page.

issues.text: Game::Dispose() raises Disposed on every call, including after an early return.
An exception during Dispose(true) leaves the game not disposed; a later Dispose() restarts the teardown.
ContentManager::Unload() clears the cache without disposing owned assets.
ResetElapsedTime() is a no-op under the fixed step, whereas XNA 4.0 zeroes the next tick's elapsed time in both modes.
GameComponent::Dispose(true) does not remove the component from Game.Components (XNA 4.0 does).
DrawableGameComponent does not follow device creation/disposal (OnDeviceCreated unsubscribed).
IsRunningSlowly hysteresis is untested and differs from XNA 4.0's heuristic.
